name: Phong Nha Cave
kicker: Boat ride into a river cave
summary: Use the morning for this, and skip it if you wanted a dry walk. From the Tourism Center a boat runs down the Son River, then you row about 1,200 metres of a cave the park measures at 7,729 metres. The visit is about two and a half hours. The entrance is 150,000 VND. The boat is 700,000 VND for up to 12 people. Paradise Cave is not on this ticket.
heroCaption: Tourist boats waiting at the mouth of Phong Nha Cave

notice.title: The entrance ticket is not the boat
notice.body: You pay 150,000 VND to enter. The boat is another 700,000 VND for the round trip, for up to 12 people. Without the boat you do not go in.

body: Buy the ticket at the Phong Nha–Ke Bang Tourism Center and take a boat number at the pier on the left. The boat runs down the Son River for about 30 minutes. The engine goes off, and the crew rows you about 1,200 metres into a cave the park measures at 7,729 metres. On that water the park names a Goddess of Mercy, a sandbank it calls Tien Sa, and a dry chamber it calls Bi Ky. On the way back a composite walkway goes through two dry branches of this same cave, Tien Cave and Royal Palace Cave. The park names a Golden Bell and a King’s Bed there.

Tien Son is not those dry branches. It sits about 100 metres above this cave, on the same pier, up nearly 600 steps. The cave is 980 metres long. You may walk about 400 metres from the entrance. The park then describes a drop of about 10 metres and a further stretch it keeps closed. The Vietnamese Tien Son page prints an entrance of 80,000 VND a person, and children under 1.3 metres are free. The English boat page does not print that line. Both pages price the shared boat at 750,000 VND a trip, instead of 700,000, for up to 12 people. Ask which entrance you are charged before you climb.

The park describes the river as jade-green in the dry season and reddish in the rainy season. It does not name those months. Give the cave a morning. The summer board runs from 07:15 to 16:30 and the winter board from 07:30 to 15:45, and you need to ask which one is posted that day. Skip this if you wanted the wooden walkway. That is Paradise Cave, on its own ticket. Skip it too if you hoped to see Son Doong the same day. The 4,500-metre kayak uses this cave and is a different booking: 1,700,000 VND a person. The night tour is named and not priced.

figures.caption: The boat inside the mouth, with the daylight behind it
figures.alt: A tour boat on the water inside the entrance of Phong Nha Cave

gettingThere: The visit starts at the Tourism Center. After you pay, the pier is on the left, and the park’s about two and a half hours includes the ride on the Son River. How long it takes to reach that counter from a bed in the village is check on arrival.

legs.heading: From the Tourism Center
legs.body: Walk to the pier on the left. The boat then runs downstream for about 30 minutes before it enters the cave.

legs.heading: From Dong Hoi
legs.body: The park puts the cave about 50 km from Dong Hoi city. The minutes are check on arrival.

hours: Summer 07:15–16:30. Winter 07:30–15:45. The park does not name the months.
closed: Open daily. No weekly closing day is published.
admissionNote: Entrance 150,000 VND a person. Children under 1.3 m are free for that entrance. The boat is 700,000 VND a round trip for up to 12 people, not a per-person fare. With Tien Son included, the boat is 750,000 VND a trip on both the English boat page and the Vietnamese Tien Son page. The Vietnamese page also prints a Tien Son entrance of 80,000 VND a person, children under 1.3 m free. The English page does not print that line. Ask at the counter whether you pay both entrances or only one. A Vietnamese guide is 300,000 VND for one cave or 400,000 for two. An English guide is 400,000 VND for one cave or 500,000 for two. No second publisher confirmed these dong figures. The 4,500-metre adventure is 1,700,000 VND a person and includes pickup in Phong Nha town, a light meal in the cave, the tickets, a guide, rescue staff, and a helmet, lamp, life jacket, and sandals. VAT is extra. Children aged 10 and above may join with a parent and the operator’s approval. Groups run from 3 to 20. The boat page names a night tour and does not price it.
